about: The reviewed source of the public course index (docs/adr/038-public-course-index.md), read by spike/scripts/build_public_course_index.py. Only what the lesson data does not state: where each OET fact and exam method is taught (an utterance, board or block id of the lesson; the time is resolved on every build), what the docs record about each lesson's source session, topics that continue in another lesson, and topics for the topic index that no section title or term box names. Every line is faithful to the narration at its anchor. Every built lesson has an entry, even an empty one. Listening facts are numbers of docs/listening-facts.md; other facts are keys of `facts` below.

facts.reading-grade-b: The target is Grade B, a score of 350.
facts.reading-thirty-of-42: About 30 of the 42 Reading questions correct usually gives Grade B; grade boundaries change a little between test sessions.
facts.reading-timing: Reading lasts 60 minutes: Part A has 15 minutes, timed on its own; Parts B and C share 45 minutes.
facts.reading-part-a: Part A has four short texts and 20 questions.
facts.reading-part-b: Part B has six short workplace texts of 100 to 150 words, one question each.
facts.reading-part-c: Part C has two long texts of about 800 words, with 16 questions of four options.
facts.reading-part-a-time-plan: Part A time plan: three minutes to skim the four texts, then the questions in order (two minutes for the matching questions).
facts.reading-part-a-guide: 15 of the 20 Part A questions is a guide within the Grade B target.
facts.reading-pencils: On the paper test, mark with a pen or a pencil; highlighters are not allowed.
facts.reading-shade: On the paper test, Part B and C answers are shaded with a 2B pencil, and only a shaded circle counts.
facts.writing-grammar-assessed: Grammar is part of how the OET letter is assessed.
facts.writing-vocabulary-range: Assessors look at the range of vocabulary in the letter.
facts.writing-letter-length: An OET letter is 180 to 200 words.
facts.writing-one-task: Writing has one task: a letter written from case notes, to another health professional or to a person who helps with the patient's care (writing-facts 1).
facts.writing-profession: The Writing task is specific to your profession: a nurse writes a Nursing task, a doctor a Medicine task (writing-facts 2).
facts.writing-letter-types: The letter is usually a referral, a discharge or a transfer letter; OET also names advice letters (writing-facts 3).
facts.writing-time: Writing takes 45 minutes: 5 minutes of reading time, then 40 minutes of writing time (writing-facts 4).
facts.writing-reading-only: The 5 minutes of reading time are for reading only: no writing, underlining or circling (writing-facts 5).
facts.writing-notes-during-writing: During the 40 minutes you can look at the task and the case notes again at any time (writing-facts 6).
facts.writing-six-criteria: Six criteria assess the letter, the same for every profession (writing-facts 8).
facts.writing-score-scale: Each sub-test is scored from 0 to 500 (writing-facts 12).
facts.writing-grade-b: Grade B is a score of 350 to 440 (writing-facts 12).
facts.writing-ielts: OET's own table compares grade B with IELTS 7.0 to 7.5 (writing-facts 13).
facts.writing-word-guide: 180 to 200 words is a guide for the body, not a strict limit, with no automatic penalty (writing-facts 14).
facts.writing-length-signals: Much longer usually means something the reader does not need; much shorter usually means something important is missing (writing-facts 15).
facts.writing-body-counted: Only the body of the letter, its paragraphs, is counted (writing-facts 16).
facts.writing-computer-counter: On computer, the word counter counts every word typed, not only the body (writing-facts 17).
facts.writing-style: The style is clinical and factual, with polite language and no personal feelings (writing-facts 21).
facts.writing-address: Copy the reader's name and address from the task (writing-facts 24).
facts.writing-re-line: The Re line gives the patient's full name and date of birth (writing-facts 26).
facts.writing-sign-off: Sign with a job title, not your own name (writing-facts 25).
facts.writing-criteria-scores: Purpose is scored out of 3; each of the other five criteria is scored out of 7, on its own (writing-facts 9).
facts.writing-grade-b-profile: For grade B, you need at least 2 out of 3 for Purpose and at least 5 out of 7 for each of the other five criteria (writing-facts 11).
facts.writing-purpose: Purpose: the reader sees at once why you are writing; the purpose is stated clearly at the start and expanded with more detail at the end of the letter (writing-facts 18, 30).
facts.writing-content: Content: what this reader needs to continue care, with nothing important missing and the case notes represented accurately (writing-facts 19).
facts.writing-conciseness: Conciseness and Clarity: only the information the reader needs, and the case summarised and presented clearly (writing-facts 20).
facts.writing-organisation: Organisation: one topic per paragraph, the most important information first; simply following the order of the case notes is a weakness (writing-facts 22, 40).
facts.writing-language: Language: grammar, vocabulary, spelling, punctuation and sentence structure that make the meaning clear (writing-facts 23).
facts.writing-abbreviations: Abbreviate for the reader and do not overdo it; abbreviations better known than their full form, such as MRI, BMI, CT and ECG, can be used (writing-facts 21, 38).
facts.writing-no-fixed-layout: There is no one required layout for the letter (writing-facts 24).
facts.writing-spelling: Spelling does not need to be perfect for grade B (writing-facts 43).
facts.writing-letter-date: The letter's date is the date the paper gives at the start ("Assume that today's date is ..."), never a date from the notes; above or below the reader's address, written in full (writing-facts 44).
facts.writing-unnamed-reader: "Yours faithfully" goes with "Dear Sir or Madam" when the reader's name is not known (writing-facts 27).
facts.writing-closing-sentence: A closing sentence commonly thanks the reader or offers contact; "Thank you for ..." and "Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions" are both acceptable, neither required (writing-facts 39; ADR 040 decision 5).
facts.writing-paragraphs: One topic in each paragraph; there is no fixed number of paragraphs (writing-facts 40).
facts.writing-fit-the-case: Full marks for Purpose need writing fitted to the case, not learnt phrases (writing-facts 33).
facts.writing-opening-verbs: "I am writing to refer" does not fit every letter: other verbs fit other tasks (writing-facts 32).

methods.name: Skimming
methods.text: Read all four texts quickly first, by their headings, bullet points, tables, bold and italics; the path is highlighted.

methods.name: The Part A question method
methods.text: For each question: the four texts as a map, the question and its keywords, try it first, rule out the texts that cannot hold the answer, then zoom into the one that does and find the answer in its exact form (ADR 026).

reading-03-part-b.session: The Reading Part B session. The instructor taught on official OET sample texts, which are excluded; the lesson applies his method to the practice set oa-set-rb-0001 (ADR 026).

methods.name: The QAT method
methods.text: Question, Answers, Text: read the question and its three options, with their keywords, before the text.

methods.name: The Part B question method
methods.text: The question and its keywords, the three options, try it first, then the extract: keyword pairs, the paraphrase of the right option, a reason for each wrong option, and the answer confirmed (ADR 026).

reading-04-part-c.session: The Reading Part C session, split at the start of Text 2: this lesson teaches Text 1, and reading-05-part-c-2 is built from the rest (ADR 026 amendment of 2026-10-08).

methods.name: Opinion signals
methods.text: A writer's view shows in four signals: opinion words, hedges, words of emotion or judgement, and the main clause that holds the view.

methods.name: The QTA method
methods.text: Question, Text, Answers: read the stem without the options, read the paragraph it points to and answer in your own words, then read the four options.

methods.name: The Part C question method
methods.text: In the order of the text, paragraph by paragraph: the question alone, the paragraph it is about, your own answer, the four options, try it first, the paraphrase of the right option, a reason for each wrong option, then the answer confirmed (ADR 026).

methods.name: The attitude scale
methods.text: For a question about a view: a line from negative to positive, a marker moved as the evidence is read, and each option placed on it.

methods.name: Signposts
methods.text: Signposts tell you that a new point, or the next question, is coming.

methods.name: Signal words
methods.text: Contrast words such as but, however, yet and nevertheless: the main point often comes after them.

writing-01-overview.session: Writing Session 1 of the Persian Writing course, «جلسه رایتینگ: مقدمه‌ای بر رایتینگ» (Writing: an introduction), the first of the recorded Writing sessions; its official OET sample is replaced by our sample oa-ws-med-0001 at oetacademy-exercises 5320d19 (ADR 040).

facts.note: a job title, such as Doctor

methods.name: Five steps towards successful writing
methods.text: Grammar, then vocabulary, then the assessment criteria, then the general Writing lessons, then practice on your own profession's tasks; and first, look at one or two sample tasks and their model letters.

methods.name: The three parts of the case-notes paper
methods.text: The setting (today's date, who you are, the patient), the case notes, and the Writing Task (letter type, reader, purpose).

methods.name: Relevant or not
methods.text: Keep the notes this reader needs, such as the patient's job when a cause at work is asked about; leave out the rest, such as hobbies.

methods.name: The teacher's word-count advice
methods.text: Ten or twelve words more or fewer do no harm; what matters is that the reader gets everything they need, nothing they do not, and less important points briefly.

topics.topic: Case notes and the Writing Task
Word count of the letter body

writing-02-assessment-criteria.session: Writing Session 2 of the Persian Writing course, «جلسه رایتینگ: معیار های ارزیابی» (Writing: the assessment criteria); its official OET sample and the photo of OET's criteria table are replaced by our sample oa-ws-med-0002 (and short parts of oa-ws-nur-0001, oa-ws-nur-0002, oa-ws-med-0003) at oetacademy-exercises 5320d19, and an own-words criteria table (ADR 040).

facts.note: a job title, such as Doctor

methods.name: Read the paper in this order
methods.text: The setting first, then the Writing Task, then the case notes line by line; ask who the reader is and what they will do.

methods.name: Expanding the purpose (the teacher's method)
methods.text: Say briefly in the opening why you are writing and what you ask; expand it straight after, in the next paragraph; give the requests in detail at the end.

methods.name: Keep, keep briefly or leave out
methods.text: For each note, ask what this reader will do with it: lines that only look related are left out; lines that explain the problem are kept briefly.

methods.name: The teacher's word-count advice
methods.text: Ten or twelve words more or fewer do no harm; what matters is that the reader gets everything they need, nothing they do not, and less important points briefly.

methods.name: The teacher's advice on style
methods.text: Never firstly, secondly or finally in the letter; fortunately or unfortunately at most once, and never about a patient's habits.

writing-03-letter-structure.session: Writing Session 3 of the Persian Writing course, «جلسه رایتینگ: ساختار نامه» (Writing: letter structure); its official OET sample (letter and case notes) is replaced by our samples oa-ws-nur-0001 (main), oa-ws-med-0002 (the dates) and oa-ws-nur-0003 (the address, greeting and Re line) at oetacademy-exercises 5320d19 (ADR 040). The teacher's exam-date rule is dropped by the owner (ADR 044).

facts.note: a job title, such as Nurse

methods.name: Where each part comes from
methods.text: The date from the date line at the top of the paper; the reader's name, address and the purpose from the Writing Task; the Re line from the patient details; the body from the notes; the request from the plan.

methods.name: Setting out the address
methods.text: Copy it from the Writing Task exactly, one part on each line, from the person to the town, keeping every capital letter.

methods.name: Expanding the purpose (the teacher's method)
methods.text: Say briefly at the start why you are writing and what you ask; expand it straight after, in the next paragraph; give the requests in detail at the end.

methods.name: From the plan to the request
methods.text: Turn each line of the plan into a polite request, keeping its date, what to do and when; report what the patient said at its exact degree.

topics.topic: The date at the top of the letter
The request at the end of the letter

writing-04-introduction.session: Writing Session 4 of the Persian Writing course, «نحوه نگارش Introduction» (Writing: introduction); every example on its slides is of unknown origin and is replaced by the openings of our six samples (oa-ws-med-0001 to -0003, oa-ws-nur-0001 to -0003) at oetacademy-exercises 5320d19 (ADR 040). The letter to a patient's relative (slides 15-16) and the pharmacy aside are dropped; the teacher's "Dear Doctor" for an unnamed reader is replaced by "Dear Sir or Madam ... Yours faithfully" (ADR 040 decision 7).

methods.name: One clear opening sentence (the teacher's method)
methods.text: Put the patient, the problem and what you ask in one clear sentence, two at most, and fit it to each case.

methods.name: Expanding the purpose (the teacher's method)
methods.text: Say briefly in the opening what you ask; expand it straight after, in the next paragraph; give each request in full at the end, never the same sentence twice.

methods.name: Personal details in the opening (the teacher's method)
methods.text: A personal detail, such as the patient's job, goes into the opening only if this reader needs it.

methods.name: Time words counted from today (the teacher's method)
methods.text: Turn the paper's dates into words counted from the letter's date: today, this morning, since yesterday.

methods.name: Five questions to plan the opening (the teacher's method)
methods.text: Who, what, when, where and why, answered from the paper; one sentence or two.
